title: ACS Trace → OCSF event-class mapping
description: Normative mapping from ACS hooks and decisions to OCSF (Open Cybersecurity Schema Framework) event classes. v0.1.0 conformance requires that a deployment emitting OCSF for the Trace pillar uses these class UIDs and severity rules verbatim. Class UIDs, class names and activity IDs are those of OCSF 1.9.0.

step_to_class.description: Map ACS step methods to OCSF class UIDs. Every step event carries the step's request_id at unmapped.acs.request_id, the same value as the OTel attribute acs.request_id.

activity_id.description: OCSF activity_id within the class (e.g., 1=Logon, 2=Logoff for Authentication).

steps/preCompact._note: Compaction is a derived-data write into the agent's working context — modeled as Datastore Activity with a custom activity_id for the compaction subtype.

steps/subagentStart._note: Subagent spawn opens a new session — modeled as Authentication/Logon for OCSF symmetry with sessionStart.

steps/skillRegister._note: Registration admits a skill to the component set and persists its definition ref and digest to the AgBOM. It is modeled as Device Inventory Info, the class agbom/* uses, with activity_id 2 (Collect).

steps/skillLoad._note: OCSF defines Module Activity as a process loading or unloading a module, and its required module object is the skill itself — not Process Activity, which needs a launched or terminated process that a skill load does not have; keeping loads off 1007 lets a reader tell a skill loading from the tool calls its actions raise.

decision_class.description: Decisions (deny/modify/ask/defer) are emitted as Detection Finding events. 'allow' is normally emitted as Application Activity with informational severity rather than as a finding, unless the deployment elects to record allows as findings for full audit symmetry.

profiles.description: OCSF profiles a decision event lists in metadata.profiles. The Security Control profile defines disposition_id, which Detection Finding does not define on its own.

disposition_mapping.description: OCSF disposition_id for decision events, keyed by ACS disposition. It records the Guardian's verdict, not the enforced outcome, which only the Observed Agent sees (Specification §6.4). A Guardian MUST NOT emit an OCSF decision event for a decision it finished after the negotiated timeout, because v0.1.0 has no OCSF form for the decision failure that would sit beside it. 99 (Other) means OCSF has no matching value. The disposition attribute carries the OCSF caption for 1, 2 and 14, and the ACS disposition name for 99. The allow entry applies when the deployment records allows as Detection Findings.

acs_fields.description: Decision facts with no OCSF attribute of their own. Each is carried under unmapped.acs with the response field's name whenever the response carries it, so the OCSF event holds the same facts as the OTel acs.decision event. request_id joins the decision to the step event it gated. policy_references keeps its object form, so it needs no padding rule. OCSF does not validate unmapped, so each field takes the type and pattern of its definition in response-envelope.json.

severity_mapping.description: OCSF severity_id values for decision events, keyed by ACS disposition.

provenance_metadata.description: When Provenance is attached to the originating hook, the OCSF event MUST carry provenance facts in 'enrichments' (an OCSF-recognized extensibility field). Each enrichment carries name='acs_provenance_*' and value={origin, source_id, ...}. v0.1 carries factual provenance in enrichments; trust classification is computed by the Guardian against local policy and is not a v0.1 enrichment (see §7.1).
